n: Freeports, safe deposit boxes and bearer instruments
ds: Value is parked and moved in forms that hide ownership and leave thin transaction trails: high-value goods in free ports or bonded storage, contents of safe deposit boxes, and bearer shares or other bearer instruments. Title can change hands without goods moving or any bank payment, so owners are obscured and value can be transferred or revalued on paper. Cash used to buy bearer instruments or fill boxes breaks the link to the original source.

rat: Safe deposit boxes at branches and goods in free ports or bonded storage, with bearer instruments bought for cash; title and value shift without bank payments.

ind.n: Art or collectibles held in free ports without display or trade
ind.cx: Art, wine, precious metals or collectibles remain in a free-port or bonded warehouse for long periods with no display, sale or loan.
ind.ds: Artworks are acquired and stored long term in free ports with no movement, display or documented purpose.

ind.cx: Customer rents a large or multiple safe deposit boxes with no clear need, or in a branch far from home or work.
ind.ds: Physical storage of unknown assets with limited visibility.

ind.cx: Bearer shares or bearer negotiable instruments hold the stored goods, or transfer in place of registered title.
ind.fp: Legacy bearer shares may be immobilised or custodied under regulation.
ind.ds: Entity has issued, or may issue, bearer shares or warrants transferable without registration.

ind.n: High-value asset held through opaque vehicle
ind.cx: Stored high-value goods are owned by a company, trust or foundation whose controller is not apparent to the storage operator or bank.
ind.fp: Privacy-motivated and estate-planning holdings can be lawful; verify beneficial ownership.
ind.ds: Property, art, vessels or other valuables are acquired or held via a company, trust or storage arrangement with concealed beneficial owners.

ind.n: Payments to or from free-trade zones and tax-free ports
ind.cx: Payments for goods or storage involve free-trade zones or tax-free ports with no link to the buyer, seller or goods origin.
ind.ds: Transfers linked to zones known for tobacco diversion.

ind.n: Provenance gaps or documents inconsistent with object history
ind.cx: Provenance papers for stored objects have gaps, conflict with each other or with the object's recorded history.
ind.ds: Missing ownership chain, 1970-era gap or fake certificates.

ind.n: High-value purchases paid in cash, crypto or non-standard funds
ind.cx: Goods placed in storage were bought with cash, virtual assets or funds from an unrelated third party.
ind.fp: Some buyers legitimately pay with cash or crypto; verify source of funds.
ind.ds: High-value assets are bought with cash, crypto, third-party or otherwise non-standard funding.

ind.n: Frequent purchase of monetary instruments in small amounts
ind.cx: Many small purchases of money orders, bearer bonds or similar instruments, often with cash, to stay under identification limits.
ind.fp: Some customers lack bank accounts and use instruments for rent or bills.
ind.ds: Multiple money orders, drafts, prepaid cards or cheques purchased with cash in sub-threshold amounts.

ind.n: Stored goods change title or are revalued repeatedly with no physical movement
ind.cx: A chain of related-party sales of a painting or bullion in a free port that drives up recorded value without cash movement.
ind.fp: Dealers, collectors and investment funds legitimately trade stored stock without moving it. Concern is a chain of related-party sales or valuations that diverge from the market.
ind.ds: Ownership of goods held in secure storage passes between parties, or declared value changes sharply on entry, exit or transfer, while the items stay in place.

ind.n: Safe deposit box access clustered around cash deposits or withdrawals
ind.cx: Repeated box access shortly before or after large cash transactions or foreign currency exchange.
ind.fp: Customers sometimes keep cash savings or valuables in boxes for ordinary reasons, and visits may coincide with legitimate banking.
ind.ds: Box visits coincide in time with large cash deposits, cash withdrawals, or purchases of cash-like instruments at the same institution.

ctl.ds: Applies enhanced checks to operators, counterparties, storage rationale and transactions that involve free-trade zones and free ports, including facility operator controls. It addresses the opacity and reduced oversight these locations can offer.

Obtains independent valuations, appraisals or comparable-sale evidence for high-value assets, collateral and traded goods, and escalates large variances. It reveals deliberately mispriced assets used to move or conceal value.

Monitors specialised products such as insurance, securities, safe deposit and prepaid instruments for surrender, free delivery, overpayment, assignment, matched trades and unusual access. It catches product-specific abuse.

Applies additional information gathering, corroboration, monitoring and senior review to relationships or transactions assessed as higher risk, covering purpose, expected activity, ownership and funds. The depth is proportionate to the risk drivers identified.

Identifies the natural persons who ultimately own or control a legal entity or arrangement and verifies them using independent registers and documents, looking through intermediate layers. It is the core defence against anonymity achieved through layered or opaque structures.

Requires nominee shareholders, directors and signatories to declare their status and name the person they act for, and declines or immobilises bearer instruments. It limits the use of nominees and bearer forms to conceal the real controller.

Alerts on unusual countries, corridors, deposit locations and geolocation dispersion relative to the customer profile or on activity near designated risk regions. It focuses review on geographic anomalies.

Requires documentary evidence of origin, legal sourcing, custody and conformity with responsible-sourcing standards, including for informal or recycled supply. It keeps illicitly sourced goods from entering the financed or traded chain.

ctl.n: Lifestyle and high-value purchase consistency review
ctl.ds: Compares observed spending, luxury and asset purchases and personal-type use of business funds with documented income and wealth during periodic reviews and alerts. It highlights unexplained affluence that may indicate illicit income.

Obtains and tests documentary evidence of where the money for a transaction, deposit or capital injection comes from, particularly when value exceeds thresholds or the customer profile. It reduces the chance that illicit proceeds are accepted without explanation.

ctl.n: Cash exchange, declaration and courier checks
ctl.ds: Collects identification for cash exchange, cross-checks cross-border cash declarations, screens freight, mail and cash-in-transit use and applies courier intelligence. It addresses bulk cash movement across borders.
Detects repeated transactions placed just below reporting or approval limits, tuned by band and window per segment. It counters deliberate splitting designed to avoid scrutiny.

Cross-checks asset ownership, title history, security registrations and registry changes against official registers, including for changes close to designation or transaction dates. It confirms that the person presenting an asset genuinely owns it.

Aggregates cash and other activity by customer, related party, account, branch, channel and day so that splitting across touchpoints cannot evade review, supported by a single customer view. It gives analysts a holistic picture of exposure.
